The trade

Every memory has one owner. Sell it and it's gone, the way the dead are gone. People bring you

first kisses, last mornings, things they'd rather not name. You have a loupe, a scale, a feel

for what a thing is really worth, and rent due at the end of the week.

But a memory is not always what it looks like. A bright first kiss can hide a grief. Dig past

the surface, or trade on it and hope. Looking closer costs the seller's patience, and some

things wear thin when you handle them.

The two markets

The Bright Exchange trades in cherished things, in the open, for honest margins. The Shadow

Ledger pays far better, and asks that you keep it quiet. The elite pay handsomely for other

people's suffering. The Bureau has opinions about that, and sends people who don't show a badge.

Neither road is free. A clean name draws steady trade and thin profits. A dark one draws money,

raids, and a kind of customer you can't always turn away. Most keepers walk the line. The line

is the game.

The people

Twenty regulars with lives, families, and reasons. They come back. What you buy from them

changes what comes back through your door. A cheerful seller who keeps selling her bright

mornings will, one visit at a time, stop being cheerful. You'll watch it happen. You did it.

The Night

Something happened on this street, and nobody will say what. It's in the drawer labels, in the

worn chair, in how some regulars look at the door before they knock. Read people's memories,

pencil in what you believe they were to it, and let the truth set in ink. Twenty-five endings.

One of them is the whole of it.

The shop is yours

- Appraise layered memories with loupe and scale. The surface pays. The truth sells.

- Haggle in real coins on a real counter. Mask what needs hiding. Pour out what you can't keep.

- Fully voiced: every seller, every buyer, every ending, and the one who reads you the story.

- A run takes an evening. The truth takes longer.

Hammered Heroes is a roguelite about recruiting a rowdy band of fantasy heroes and sending them brawling down a dungeon that runs deeper than anyone sober should attempt. You don't pilot a single hero — you command the whole drunken expedition. Pick who joins, what they specialize in, where you descend, and how you spend every coin. Then the band fights it out in real time while you read the battlefield and make the calls that keep them standing.

Every run starts with one free founding hero and a fistful of gold. Every run ends differently.

Command the band, don't babysit it
Your heroes hold the line, pick their targets, and swing on their own. Your job is the part that actually wins runs: building a party whose damage types cover the road ahead, choosing the right boon after every floor, training skill points into the build you're chasing, and knowing when to spend gold on a fresh recruit instead of a heal. Get the composition right and your band steamrolls. Get greedy and the whole expedition wipes in the dark.

A roster where no two parties are alike
Start with a free founding hero and earn the rest by playing — slay enough goblins to recruit the Wizard, clear graveyards for the Death Knight, raze monster dens for the Demolitionist. Glass-cannon Sorcerers that start frail and end devastating. Holy Templars that scourge the undead. Beastmasters, Pyromancers, Gladiators, Assassins — each with its own stats, damage type, and a kit of signature abilities.

Biomes that fight back
Descend through stone halls, frozen wastes, haunted graveyards, trap-laced mines, sunken marshes, and burning underworlds. Each biome has a signature monster that dictates how you should fight there — frost to chill the swarms, holy to put down the undead, fire to melt the frost-numb, arcane to shatter the armored. Bring the wrong party and the dungeon teaches you why.

A descent with teeth
Bosses guard the deep floors. Chromatic dragons stand as the run's great walls, each tougher than anything before it. Reach the bottom and a final tyrant waits — fell it to win, or press on into Endless and see how deep your band can really go.

Die smarter, not just again
When the band falls, you keep what matters. Fallen wanderers leave Echoes behind — spend them on permanent upgrades that make every future expedition tougher. Every class grows stronger the more you play it, carried across all runs forever. Each wipe sends you back to the tavern a little stronger, a little wiser, and ready to go again.

The dungeon's deep, the ale's flowing, and somebody has to clear it. Might as well be hammered.

Hamstr Protocol is a first-person bio-mining simulator where you build, manage, and scale a mining operation powered by hamsters.

Start in a garage with a few rigs and a handful of runners. Assemble your hardware by hand, keep your hamsters fed, control the heat, and turn a small operation into an industrial-scale bio-mining business.

ASSEMBLE


Experience tactile, first-person interaction. Pick up, carry, and place every piece of hardware by hand. Every component matters in your quest for the ultimate mining setup.

SCALE


The more you scale, the harder it gets to keep everything under control. Manage heat, noise, and hunger as you expand from a small garage setup into a massive industrial operation.

LIQUIDATE


Money never sleeps. Use your in-game ATM to track market trends and trade your HAM for USD at the terminal. Reinvest your profits to break the system or save up for the next big upgrade.

CORE FEATURES

  • Hamster-powered rigs - Put your runners to work and pair hamster power with high-end hardware.

  • Hands-on building - Pick up, place, and manage your equipment directly in first person.

  • Thermal management - Heat can destroy your operation. Keep your rigs cool or pay the price.

  • Hamster management - Keep your runners fed and your operation moving.

  • Fully interactive PC - Manage key parts of your operation through a functional in-game computer.

  • Garage to industry - Start small and build toward an increasingly ridiculous industrial operation.

  • Something doesn't add up - But that's a problem for later.

Behind the warm bricks and the proper wood-fired oven, past the smell of fresh dough, is a tight game of precision and margins. A game where a good night is measured in quality food, delivered well, and with books that end up in the black rather than in the red.

Hand Stretched puts you and up to two friends in charge of the pizzeria, running 6 minute shifts, each in one of three key roles: Chef, Waiter or Manager. Play together over LAN or online, each on your own machine — or split into two shops and go three against three, the same customers walking through both doors, best profit wins. Nobody is burying you in orders. You are given just enough that doing it well is the whole trick. Serve hot, waste little, keep the customers from wandering off, and turn a profit whilst rent, wages, and stock costs quietly eat away at your bottom line.

PICK A ROLE, PULL YOUR WEIGHT

Three jobs, one team. The Chef works the oven: stretch the dough, add the toppings, and retrieve from the oven before it burns to a crisp. The Waiter runs the floor: seat parties before they give up and leave, take orders, pour the drinks, and get the food out while it is still hot to earn a tip. The Manager keeps the business breathing: order the stock, watch the till, and settle a complaint before it becomes a walkout. The team part is the hand-offs. A pizza going cold on the pass is a Waiter who was elsewhere. A Chef stood idle is a Manager who let the cheese run out.

RIGHT FIRST TIME, OR SENT BACK

A game of details, not speed. Put the wrong topping on and serve it anyway, the table will notice and you'll be making it again or eating a refund. Serve a pizza cold and you can wave the tip goodbye. Deliver a whole table's order in one trip and you might see a bit extra for the trouble. Every slip up has a price: a remake costs you time and a binned base, a complaint costs you a discount, and both come straight off your bottom line. Do it cleanly and a busy stretch becomes a genuinely satisfying, and profitable, shift.

MIND THE MARGINS

You pay for your ingredients the moment you buy them, so every shift opens in the red and you sell your way out. Meanwhile the rent and wages tick up whether a soul walks in or not. Waste eats your margin, refunds eat your margin, and only happy tables leave a tip, so keeping people cheerful is not manners, it is money. Your star rating rides on it: a healthy margin and not a single walkout is what separates a proud three stars from a shrug.

STOCK, SPEED AND THE PRICE OF PANIC

Run out of dough mid-shift and the whole line stops, so the Manager is forever reading the shelves. Order too little and you stock out. Order too much and that is cash sitting in the fridge. And when you have cut it too fine, you can pay for a faster supplier: the cheap van takes its time, the express one turns up in seconds and helps itself to your margin on the way past. Leave it too late, shelves empty and the overdraft maxed, and the night ends early with the shutters down and the business bankrupt.

THE OVERTIME QUESTION

When the clock hits zero with tables still waiting and pizzas still in the oven, you get one call: shut now, or buy another 15, 30 or 45 seconds at time and a half wages. The doors are closed, so no new custom is coming. It only pays off if you can turn the people already sat down into settled bills before the borrowed time runs out. Call it right and it is the difference between a good night and a great one. Call it wrong and you have paid premium wages to watch a table leave anyway.

SHORT SHIFTS, LONG MEMORIES

A shift lasts six minutes. Long enough to test a plan, short enough that you will always want one more. Pace quickens the further you climb, the arrivals coming faster and the patience running shorter, and your best nights go on the leaderboards, where you will learn in time that your friends are not quite as good as they claim.

TOGETHER, OR AT EACH OTHER'S THROATS

Play solo and run all three roles yourself. Team up with up to two friends and split the load (or the blame!) — each of you at your own machine, over LAN or online. Cooking alongside someone brings its own wrinkle: with a second pair of hands on the line the oven wants watching properly, and a pizza nobody turns halfway will scorch. Or go shop against shop, three a side, where the only thing better than a clean shift is watching the other lot fumble theirs with the very same orders.

FACES ON, GLOVES OFF

In LAN or friends only play, every player gets a live kitchen cam and voice chat, so the whole team is on screen and reacting in real time. It is the closest thing to a real kitchen without the burns, and it turns a friends night or a LAN into something properly daft. When everyone can see your face, there is nowhere for the blame to hide.

FROM OUR KITCHEN TO YOUR COMPUTER

Hand Stretched started as a pure passion project. I have a separate, full-time career, but I wanted a hobby project that I could build for and with my young children. Every mechanic, level design, and core concept came directly from our brainstorming sessions at the kitchen table. 

Because I am a solo developer, juggling a full-time job and family life, AI tools served as our digital force multiplier. It allowed us to generate (to our vision) the visual assets, the code and build the website needed to bring our family's game idea to life, whilst music and some code elements were sourced from online sources by generous contributors who license their work for anyone to use (full credits in the game - you guys rock!). We are incredibly proud of what we built together, and we hope you feel the heart (and the stress!) that went into every shift.

Every Battle Is a Three-Hand Showdown

Forget traditional poker.

Handslayer is a poker-inspired RPG roguelike where every battle is fought with three poker hands instead of one. Carefully arrange your cards, predict your opponent's strategy, and outplay them in tactical PvE battles where every decision matters.

Master poker hands, adapt to each encounter, and discover countless ways to build the perfect strategy.

Build Your Dream Team

Choose from many heroes across roles — Tank, Warrior, Mage, Assassin and more.

Every hero brings a unique passive ability that can completely change how you approach a fight. Stack the right combination and create broken synergies that turn ordinary poker hands into devastating plays.

Master the Power of the Four Suits

Every card contributes to more than just your poker hands.

Collecting cards of the same suit unlocks powerful battle bonuses, allowing you to specialize in completely different playstyles.

♥ Hearts — Increase your Attack and gain Lifesteal to outlast your enemies.

♦ Diamonds — Focus on Critical Chance and devastating Critical Damage for explosive attacks.

♣ Clubs — Steal more Gold and earn additional rewards to grow stronger throughout your run.

♠ Spades — Strengthen your Defense and Block Chance to withstand even the deadliest bosses.

Will you commit to a single suit or combine them to create your own strategy?

Choose Ancient Artifacts

Power always comes at a price.

At the beginning of every adventure, you'll discover mysterious Ancient Artifacts that can dramatically reshape your run. Each artifact offers unique strengths, and often equally dangerous drawbacks.

Choose wisely, adapt your strategy, and uncover powerful combinations that can completely change the way you play.

Collect Powerful Relics

Discover relics that transform every battle.

From subtle improvements to game-changing effects, relics create endless opportunities for powerful synergies. Combine them with your poker hands, suit bonuses, artifacts, and skill choices to build strategies capable of overcoming impossible odds.

Every run offers new combinations to discover.

Shop, Gear Up, and Risk It All

Spend the gold you earn in shops to buy:

• Gears that equip directly onto your heroes

• Active items you can use mid-battle

• Permanent party-wide stat boosts

Feeling bold? Enter the cursed stages. Sacrifice HP to claim high-risk relics — some of the strongest gears and buffs in the game.

Forge Your Own Path

Unlock powerful nodes in a deep Skill Tree filled with meaningful choices.

Specialize in your favorite playstyle, strengthen your preferred suit, or experiment with entirely new builds. Every node has the potential to reshape your strategy, making each adventure feel unique.

No two runs are ever the same.

Features

  • 🂡 Unique three-hand poker combat unlike traditional poker games.

  • Embark a party of 3 heroes each has unique abilities.

  • Maximizing heroes' playstyles with fitting Gears.

  • ⚔️ Strategic PvE battles against challenging enemies and bosses.

  • ♥♦♣♠ Four suit archetypes, each with unique combat bonuses and playstyles.

  • 🗿 Choose powerful Ancient Artifacts with meaningful trade-offs.

  • 💎 Collect Relics and discover game-breaking synergies.

  • 🌳 Deep Skill Tree with impactful build customization.

  • 🗺️ Branching roguelike adventures with high replayability.

  • 👑 Epic boss encounters that challenge your strategy.

  • 🔄 Endless combinations of cards, relics, artifacts, and skills.

Happy Lane: The Threshold is a first-person horror game supporting 1-4 player online co-op.

Six years ago, a lightning strike buried everything deep within the Dahang Mountains. Now, you and your companions are trapped inside a research facility that officially "never existed." Here, space constantly reconfigures, and every door leads to an unknown chamber. You must make choices based on limited information—but not every choice allows you to survive. A single misjudgment will cause "It" to emerge from the darkness instantly. Some entities cannot be fought; they can only be outsmarted by following the rules.

Collaborate with your teammates, decipher clues, and find the sole exit within this shifting architecture. Or, remain in this facility forever.

Story Background

Six years ago, a disappearance was quietly buried. Six years later, during an ordinary moment after school, the peace of Dayuan Middle School is shattered. The familiar corridors "peel away" before Betty and Hank; space fractures like a broken surface, and without warning, they fall—plummeting into a completely alien world.

They find themselves in an underground facility hidden deep in the heart of the Dahang Mountains—cold, sealed, and seemingly erased from history. The complex is filled with rusted gauges, displaced pipes, and flickering lights that blur the line between truth and deception. Every passage leads to the unknown, and every step forward is shadowed by latent danger.

Space loses its stability here; structures overlap and shift, causing cracks to appear in both reality and cognition. Faced with this nightmare, Betty begins to wonder—could all of this be connected to that incident six years ago that no one dares to mention?

But the answer doesn't matter. In this labyrinth of shifting ruins, they have only one goal: Find the exit.

Game Features

  • Solve the Puzzle, or Gamble with Your Life? Carefully observe your environment and piece together clues to find the "correct path" to the next zone. Alternatively, you can trust your intuition and push open that unknown door.

  • Ever-Changing Space The layout changes every time you enter. Rooms, corridors, and exits are randomly generated, with clue locations and paths reconfiguring constantly. No one can memorize the route; you can only rely on your immediate judgment.

  • Progression and Survival Gather resources through repeated attempts to enhance your equipment and abilities. Perhaps next time, you’ll make it a little further.

I never wanted to be the dad who says "go study."


You're an office worker in your forties. You live in Tokyo, went to a decent university, work at a decent company.
You never took entrance exams as a kid yourself. You wanted your daughter to grow up free.

...Right up until you noticed the part of you that quietly hopes she gets into a top school.

Happy Project 12 is a life-sim in which you become the father of Hinata, a fourth-grader,
and live out the three years leading to her junior high entrance exams in February of sixth grade.

Three years, 69 turns. Every weekly choice decides everything


Each turn, you decide how your daughter spends her time.

  • Have her study — Japanese, math, science, social studies. Her stats grow, her stamina drains
  • Let her play — stamina and drive come back. But that week's studying is gone

Six stats grow: STEM Knowledge, Humanities, Reading, Calculation, Reasoning and Drive.
But— a daughter whose Drive has bottomed out will not do what you tell her.
"I don't feel like it today." One sentence, and the week you planned disappears.

Mock exams: reality with nowhere to hide


Six of them in three years. National mock exams score your parenting without mercy.
Depending on her results, she moves between Class α and Class β at cram school.
Move up and she gains confidence; drop down and— dinner that week gets a little quiet.

Grades aren't the only thing that matters


In this game there is something you have to watch besides her academic ability.

It's the trust between parent and child.

What you answered when your daughter asked for help.
The face you made on the day her grades fell.
All of it adds up, never once shown to you as a number, and quietly decides how it all ends.

Because you can't see it, all you can do is believe in your own three years.

A family isn't a battle you fight alone


Your wife Naomi checks the exam forums and social media every single night.
She rides every high and low of your daughter's grades, second-guesses your decisions, and is slowly worn down.

Leave her alone and your family breaks before the exams do.
...Entrance exams are not the child's problem alone.

Over 50 story events, and 11 endings


Afternoons with friends, cram school meetings, Christmas, the walk home from a mock exam, and exam day itself.
All kinds of events unfold one after another across the three years.

And waiting beyond the final results are 11 different endings.

Getting into her first-choice school doesn't guarantee happiness.
Failing every school doesn't rule out redemption.
...What decides it isn't only her deviation score, but how you faced your daughter over three years.

Endings you reach are recorded in the ending gallery, and you can play again and again until you've filled it.

Contents


  • Three years, roughly 70 turns of main story (about one hour per playthrough)
  • 50+ story events / 11 endings (with a gallery feature)
  • Skip for already-read events, dialogue log, 10 save slots
  • Fully localized in 10 languages (Japanese / English / Simplified Chinese / Traditional Chinese / Spanish / Portuguese (Brazil) / German / French / Korean / Russian)

February, three years from now. What will your face look like as you send her off?

Harbor Water is a single-player card-based survival game built around emergency knowledge for flood disasters.

You'll guide one ordinary household as they weigh hard trade-offs against limited supplies through eight rounds of rising floodwater. Whether those resources last until the water recedes comes down to every single card in your hand.

Take Stock and Prepare for the Flood

Open every cabinet in the house and log each item of food, drinking water, and first-aid supplies. You can also buy goods from the shop against whatever may come. Every bit you set aside now is a little less panic later.

Clear Negative Conditions, Keep Illness and Hunger at Bay

Treat sickness, restore stamina, and hold thirst, hunger, and pain back from the breaking point. The moment a body gives out will drown this household sooner than the water ever could.

Call on the Neighbors for Supplies

Use various items to ask the neighbors for supplies. Whether anything comes back is entirely down to luck.

A perfect plan

Every summer of his childhood, Nico got sent to his grandparents' orchard to pick fruit up off the ground. Apples mostly. He hated it, and he never once said so, because Trudi and Klaus were so pleased to have him there that it seemed easier to tell them it was the best part of his year. He must have been convincing. They believed it for about twenty years.

Now they're too old to keep the place going, so they've signed it over to him. As far as they're concerned it's the nicest thing anyone has ever done for anybody.

He thanked them properly. He did not mention what he was actually thinking, which was that he now owned the worst summers of his life, in writing.

So he made a plan. Collect every last piece of fruit, sell all of it, sell the orchard, and never touch an apple again.

The plan survives about twenty minutes. Somewhere between the first full basket and the sight of a patch of grass with nothing whatsoever left on it, something goes wrong, and Nico starts having a good time.

The orchard does not stay empty

Clearing all six gardens finishes season one. Season two starts straight afterwards and it starts faster, and before it does you get dealt cards that change how it plays. A bigger basket. More reach on the grabber. Robots that don't slack off. One card just quietly lowers the workbench prices for the rest of the season, which sounds boring until you do the arithmetic. Twenty of them so far, and from season six on you're picking ten at a time.

The numbers move with you. Bare hands get you a piece or two at a time. By the end of a run the fruit vacuum is pulling in twenty-five a second, the last garden has seventy-nine thousand peaches lying in it, and you will clear that too.

Nico's plan was to do this once.

Two ways to clear an orchard

Both work, and the game has no opinion about which one you pick.

Switch your head off. Walk around, hold the button, watch a lawn empty. Nothing here runs on a timer, nothing can be failed, nothing is chasing you, and nobody minds if you stop and look at the trees for a while. Buy whichever upgrade has the nicest icon. Leave a robot working one garden while you wander off into another. You can play this badly for two hours and still finish it, which is not an accident.

Or take it apart. Keep collecting without a break and a streak builds; the pace steps up, the sound climbs with it, and at the top it tips over into FRENZY. Clear a quarter of a garden cleanly and it pays out for the rest of the run. Which tool suits which density, when to sell, which upgrade to buy before which other one: none of that is obvious, and all of it gets measured. The records screen remembers your best pick rate, your longest flow, how long you held Frenzy, how far you walked, and what share of the work each tool did. There are leaderboards for when you think you've solved it.

Both are built on the same idea. Every few seconds the game should be handing you something, rather than asking something of you: a basket filling up, a patch of grass going bare, a number you didn't have a minute ago. Nothing here is testing you. It's meant to be the thing you put on after a bad day, and to still be worth the two hours.

In the game

  • Six gardens, each with its own fruit and its own robot that keeps working while you're somewhere else.

  • Three tools and a workbench full of upgrades, priced so that buying one means not buying another.

  • Twelve rare finds, two per fruit, mixed in among the ordinary ones. The collection fills up as you turn them up.

  • Mastery goals for every garden, if clearing one isn't enough for you.

  • Steam achievements and leaderboards.

  • A cozy mode that hides the speed readouts and the record pop-ups, and collecting on a toggle instead of a button you hold down.

  • Ten languages, all of them voiced and subtitled, plus a colour-blind mode, free key rebinding and scalable text.

And then?

“Funny,” Nico says, somewhere in the sixth garden. “I thought I'd be happier about finishing.”

He could sell the place now. That was the plan. He's not going to sell the place, and you knew that before he did.

Dodge. Level up. Survive.

Golden wheatfields, frozen plains, burning lava, shifting desert sands, an endless Void — every battlefield has its own waves and its own boss, and its own dance of death for you.

Harvest Havoc is an auto-firing action roguelike. Your weapons lock onto the nearest enemy and fire on their own; all you do is weave through the swarm and decide which weapons and passives to take at every level-up, until each run grows into a build all its own.

⚔️ Core gameplay

🎯 Fully automatic fire — 7 weapons and 9 passives. Your weapon targets the nearest enemy by itself; you just dodge.

⭐ Weapon evolution — weapon at Lv5 + its paired passive at Lv5 → the whole barrage moves up a class, transforming damage and effects outright.

🌱 Companion building — enemies drop parts; plant three and they merge into a companion that fights on its own: snowman, flying saucer, volcano, pyramid and wheat sprout.

🧙 6 playable characters — Hooded Ranger, Warden, Gale Scout, Flame Adept, Echo Hunter and Pyro Fist, each with their own starting weapon and talent.

🗺️ 5 themed maps + 1 you draw yourself

🌾 Wheatfield — where it starts: your first fight under the cover of golden ears.

❄️ Frost Plains — the ice sends you sliding; one wrong step and you are in the middle of the pack.

🔥 Lava Cavern — a red-hot battlefield under burnt crust: damage and pressure step up sharply.

🌵 Desert Oasis — quicksand drags at you; the final stretch tests how you plan a route.

🌌 Void Arena — the endless mode, unlocked once all 4 themed maps are cleared. A boss every 3 minutes, scored on how long you last.

🎨 Custom Map — 9 painting slots in the shop: draw the map yourself and it becomes the ground you fight on. Round palette, 4 brush sizes and an eraser.

💪 Permanent progress: the longer you play, the easier it gets

Gold banks at the end of every run. Title screen → Shop:

📊 7 permanent stat perks — HP, damage, cooldown, area, pickup, armor and speed.

🎭 5 new characters

🗺️ 3 new maps

🖌️ 9 custom map slots + drawing tools

No death is wasted.

🏆 24 achievements

From "first boss down" to "shop cleared out", spread across five fronts: kills, survival, maps cleared, endless mode and custom maps.

🎮 Controls

⌨️ Full keyboard, gamepad and mouse support

👤 Single player, runs of 5 to 20 minutes

Ready to cross the wheatfield, the snow, the lava, the desert and the Void — and draw a battlefield of your own?

About This Game

Harvest Story is a casual strategy game that blends merge mechanics with survival management. On the surface, you're just dragging ingredients together on a small platform to craft fancier dishes and sell them for cash. Underneath, you're racing the clock—the landlord comes knocking every 7 days, and rent only climbs higher. The longer you want to last, the more carefully you need to plan every inch of platform space and every coin you earn.

🍳 Merge Your Way Through 200 Dishes

Start with basic crops and proteins, merge them into simple dishes, then advanced ones, and finally elaborate premium creations. The same ingredients combined in a different order can lead down an entirely different recipe tree—every run is a fresh planning puzzle.

🤖 Stop Doing Everything Yourself—Hire Robots

Five types of robots, each with their own job: auto-crafting, daily coin income, spawning more robots, tagging your priciest item for a bonus sale, and delivering fresh ingredients straight to your platform. Which ones do you invest in, when, and how many—to squeeze out the most value before rent comes due?

🧪 A Tech Tree for Going Further Next Time

Every run converts your days survived and total sales into tech points, which carry over permanently between runs. Spend them to unlock a bigger shelf, a larger crafting platform, a higher robot cap, and more—today's failure is tomorrow's comeback fund.

🏆 Chase Your Own High Score

A persistent leaderboard always reminds you how many days you lasted and how much you earned last time—every new run, you'll want to push just a little further.

Underneath the cozy farm aesthetic lies a survival challenge that demands careful planning. Can you survive the landlord's next visit?

No one tells you why.
You cut through a kingdom crowd by crowd, and the game explains itself exactly once — at the very end.



Sweep over the kingdom's people and take what they're worth — coins, blood and souls. When it sends knights and paladins to stop you, harvest them too.



Who dies first is the real decision. Some of them are worth more alive.



None of the 42 weapons is for sale. Each is carried by a named boss: beat them, take it broken off the corpse, repair it at your anvil.



Between harvests, what you harvested goes into the upgrade grid.



Bosses are bigger fights. The King fills a 3x3 piece of the field and barely takes a scratch while his court stands: cut the court down for a window, then do it again.

The story passes in short wordless scenes. The last entry in the quest log is sealed: ? ? ?
That one gets answered too. Once.

  • 42 weapons, each taken off its named boss and repaired at the anvil
  • 30 enemy types — some worth more alive than dead
  • An upgrade grid of 117 nodes and 548 ranks, and 12 permanent artifacts
  • Auto-firing attacks and 29 auto-cast skills — plays with one hand on the mouse
  • 21 achievements
  • Interface in English, Russian, and Spanish

Harvest Together is a cozy farming sim you can play alone or online with up to 4 friends. Start with a patch of soil and a dream — end up with a farm that's truly, warmly yours: animals that adore you, a dog that brings you gifts, a guestbook full of friends' notes, and a village that knows you by name.

 

🚜 BUILD YOUR FARM

Till, plant and harvest 25+ crop varieties. Raise chickens, ducks, geese, cows, goats, sheep and pigs — collect eggs, milk, wool, honey and truffles. Construct greenhouses, barns, coops, beehives, wells and wind pumps, and expand your land zone by zone.

 

🛠️ BRING THE OLD TRACTOR BACK TO LIFE

A rusty old tractor sits on your land, waiting for someone who cares. Restore it piece by piece — and once it rumbles back to life, it's yours to drive: hop in and cruise across your fields. In co-op the restoration is a farm project you complete together, and every friend can take it for a spin.

 

⏰ A FARM THAT LIVES ON REAL TIME

Crops grow in real time — even while the game is closed. And the world moves with the real calendar:

• A courier arrives every week with a Town Order — deliver it for gold, diamonds and XP.

• The Traveling Merchant rolls in twice a week with discounted seeds and one exotic seed the shop doesn't sell yet.

• Every day two of your goods become Market Specials and sell for +30%.

• On the first weekend of every month, the Harvest Festival comes to your farm: fairground stalls and a weekend-long harvest contest with bronze, silver and gold prizes.

 

🍂 SEASONS THAT MATTER (BUT NEVER LOCK YOU OUT)

Every crop and fish has a favorite season: in-season crops grow faster, in-season fish bite more often. Nothing is ever locked — plant and catch whatever you like, whenever you like. Rain waters your fields for free, fog and snow repaint the meadows, and volumetric skies make every season feel alive.

 

🎁 EVENT PASS — FREE FOR EVERYONE

Time-limited events bring a reward pass with exclusive prizes, including event-only horse variants. Every single tier is free — no paid track, no wallet required. Just play, level the pass, and claim rewards that stay on your account for good.

 

🌟 GROW YOUR FARMER

A 40-level skill tree split across four branches — Farming, Nature, Commerce and Mastery. There are never enough points for everything, so choose your path… and in co-op, skills are personal: you take Commerce while your friend goes fishing, on every farm a different build.

 

🧑‍🌾 HIRE FARMHANDS

Hire helper NPCs who water, harvest and collect for you. Upgrade their work area and pace, choose their duties — and hand them a pouch of seeds so they plant your tilled soil while you ride off on horseback.

 

🐄 ANIMALS THAT LOVE YOU BACK

Name your animals and pet them every day — as their hearts fill (0–5), their goods sell for more. Befriend your farm dog: walk it across the fields, pet it daily, and once you're close, it starts fetching you little gifts.

 

✨ EVERY HARVEST CAN SURPRISE YOU

Any harvest can mutate into Silver, Golden or Rainbow quality for a big gold premium. Any dish can come out Perfect for a bonus payout. Fertilizer and in-season crops raise your odds — everything connects.

 

👥 REAL CO-OP, NOT A SPECTATOR MODE

Friends join with a room code and share everything: one farm level, one wallet, one story. Ripening crops can merge into Giant Crops you harvest together; work fast side-by-side to fill the Team Combo meter for bonus gold. Every visitor is remembered in your farm's Guestbook — and can sign it with a note. Host permissions, in-game chat, and per-farm personal skill builds keep it fair and fun.

 

🌷 MAKE IT BEAUTIFUL, MAKE IT YOURS

Dozens of decorations — flower beds, lamps, benches, a tire swing — raise your farm's Beauty rating (0–5 ★), proudly displayed in your guestbook. Customize your farmer with outfits, hairstyles and accessories, build a stable and gallop across your land on one of four classic horses.

 

🗺️ Fully localized in 33 languages.

Harvestide is a roguelike that blends card-building with farm management. Play crop cards to plant, use spell cards to speed up growth, and construct building cards for permanent buffs—every card you play shapes your farm. But the Wither Moon descends regularly, slashing your yields, and random events can disrupt your plans at any moment. You must find your god-tier synergy before your food runs out.

Hundreds of Cards, Endless Combos

  • Crop Cards – Plant them to harvest food, but they can be destroyed by the Wither Moon.

  • Spell Cards – Instant effects: accelerate growth, boost yields, save your farm.

  • Building Cards – Permanent effects, but they take up precious worker slots.

Permanent Growth, Stronger Every Run
Spend surplus food to earn coins, use them to draw cards, permanently expand your land, and raise your limits. Your farm grows along with your skills.

Hasami is a tree pruning game where every cut cleaves through everything it crosses. Find the right angle, pull branches aside with ropes, nurture new growth, and clean endless procedural trees down to their blossom.

Every cut counts

Draw a line across a branch and everything it crosses falls into the pond. Bare wood costs you, so does dead blossom, and only living blossom pays. Look through the crown with the branch view, tie limbs aside with ropes, and let good cuts buy new growth.


A new tree every day

If you're feeling competitive, a tree is picked at random each day and given a leaderboard. Shape it, file your score, and see where you land among your friends and the world. Every round on the board keeps its replay: open one and scrub through it to see exactly how the best trees were cut.

No two trees alike

Nineteen species, each grown from a seed, each with its own garden around it. The same seed grows the same tree on any machine, so every tree can be shared and played again.


Wildlife in the garden

Herons wade the shallows, owls roost in the canopy, and dragonflies skim the pond. Raise the field camera, draw a loop round whatever catches your eye, and the photograph goes into your notebook.

“20 years ago, my father-in-law invented this board game and built it by hand, in wood. We could not produce it physically… so I turned it into a video game.”

now, HATCH'N'WALL is a digital turn-based medieval board game.

A bit of lore...

The King is dead, and his heirs now fight over the kingdom's throne.

Champion! You have been chosen by your prince to recover the royal crown hidden deep within the castle. But Beware: other champions are also racing to seize it before you. In this maze of shifting walls and treacherous hatches, use the castle's traps to block your opponents, foil their plans, and be the first to escape with the royal crown!

Game Features

  • Up to 4 knights face off in a castle. Be the unique Champion!

  • At the start of the game, each player draws a Contact Card and keeps it secret until reaching the corresponding tile. They then obtain a key, granting access to the Treasure Room, where they collect a treasure and draw a Secret Exit Card. No one knows your plan until you make your move. Bluffing is half the battle.

  • Two dice per turn — one for movement, one for action. Every roll brings you closer to your goal while sabotaging your rival.

  • 4 actions possible: build walls, trigger hatches, destroy obstacles, or use ladders. Control the maze, control the game.

  • The board is procedurally generated every game — contacts, traps and cards are shuffled each time. No two games are ever the same.

  • Want to tease your rivals? A taunt wheel is available. 

  • Play against friends in local hot seat or online multiplayer via Steam, or sharpen your tactics against AI opponents with three difficulty levels.

  • 8 knight ranks, from Squire to King's Champion: every match earns you glory

Think. Trap. Escape.

Will you be the first to break through the walls, outsmart the traps, and escape with the treasure?

— Original concept by "Boldectotor" · Video game adaptation by "Cpt.Jhon.H.Miller"

HAUNTASY: Two Modes, One Haunted Estate

HAUNTASY offers two very different ways to experience the horrors of Bigalow Estate.

THE BARON'S SEVEN-NIGHT CHALLENGE

Single-Player Survival Horror

Survive seven nights inside a haunted estate for a chance to claim $1,000,000.

Monitor paranormal activity, keep your candles burning, manage your resources, and survive until 4 AM.

Each night brings new mysteries, forgotten victims, and evidence that could uncover the truth behind the estate.

THE BARONESS' EXPERIMENT

Local Couch Co-op | Exploration | Progression

The Baroness has a different experiment in mind.

Bring a friend, create your characters, build relationships, collect equipment, and unlock powerful perks.

But the estate holds more than ghosts.

Deep beneath the grounds, the Baroness has concealed secret dungeons and a mysterious artifact.

Through Estate Excavation, dig for forgotten relics, discover treasure, battle dangerous creatures, and descend deeper into the estate's hidden past.

What has the Baroness buried beneath her estate? Can you find it?

The Baroness' Experiment launches October 29 with local couch co-op, and this is just the beginning! Expect ongoing updates with new features, deeper progression, and more secrets to uncover beneath the estate.

Sign your life away for a cool mil.

Do you believe in ghosts?

Can you survive seven nights inside Baron Bigalow's estate?

HAUNTASY is a first-person survival horror game where you accept a mysterious challenge: spend seven nights inside a haunted estate and walk away with $1,000,000.

Sounds easy.

It isn't.

From 8 PM to 4 AM, you'll have to monitor the estate through an old television, keep your candles burning, manage limited matches and resources, track paranormal activity, and repel the ghosts before they reach you.

But surviving the dead is only part of the problem.

Hunger slows you down. Your sanity can break. Rooms can become haunted. Doors and windows may not stay the way you left them. Sometimes the safest thing you can do is pray. Sometimes you'll need to fish, eat, trade, invest, or spend your last few dollars preparing for whatever comes next.

Every night pushes the estate further.

Survive the Night. Claim Your Place Among THE SURVIVORS.

Every ghost has a story.

And the deeper you make it into Baron Bigalow's challenge, the more you'll uncover about the people who died here... and why you were invited in the first place.

Build your character through perks, develop relationships, unlock memories, and slowly become better equipped to survive the later nights. Or, if you're good enough, rely on nothing but timing, resource management, and your ability to keep the ghosts out.

Seven nights. One haunted estate. One million dollars.

THIS IS YOUR HAUNTASY.

Features

  • Survive seven increasingly dangerous nights.

  • Survive alone or with a friend in 2-player couch co-op.

  • Every playthrough is different with randomized room and TV channel layouts.

  • Track paranormal activity through an old television set.

  • Relight candles to hold back the darkness.

  • Install flame sensors to reveal ghostly movement.

  • Manage matches, money, hunger, and sanity.

  • Catch over 100 species of fish to stay fed.

  • Face multiple paranormal entities, each with unique behaviors.

  • Purchase and expand the estate to uncover new haunted locations.

  • A tense blend of psychological horror, strategy, and resource management.

------------------------------------------------------------

A Note from the Developer

My mission is simple:

I want to scare you.

If I succeeded... please let me know.

DO YOU DARE TO INVESTIGATE THIS FOOTAGE?

Haunted Echoes is a raw, claustrophobic psychological horror experience captured through the lens of a bodycam. In this classified operation where everything is recorded, you are tasked with discovering anomalies where reality and nightmare blur together. But you are not alone in the dark.

KEY FEATURES

  • Raw Bodycam Perspective: With a realistic fisheye lens and a gritty helmet-mounted flashlight, you will find yourself right in the middle of a deeply claustrophobic atmosphere.

  • Reactive Threats: The mannequin figures lurking in dark corridors and abandoned lobbies are not just static objects; they are uncanny threats that could appear right behind you at any moment.

  • Atmospheric Dread: Instead of cheap jumpscares, immerse yourself in a constantly escalating psychological tension built on ambient audio and the sheer helplessness of the dark.

  • Limited Line of Sight: Your flashlight won't last forever. You can never predict what is waiting for you in the pitch-black areas where the light cannot reach.

Will you be able to follow this unlisted footage to the very end, or will you become just another echo in the dark?

Haunted House is a horror puzzle game.

You wake in a guest room of an old house, your wife Alice beside you.

Just as you are leaving, a little girl calling herself Annie appears beside the two of you, and makes a request of you.

To take Alice out of this strange mansion, you have no choice but to play Annie's game...

The oil lamp

The only light in Haunted House is the oil lamp in your hand.

The lamp burns through its oil as time passes, and being without light in a pitch black mansion is very dangerous, so pick up oil and matches as you explore.

There are also unusual things in the mansion that will chase you, so remember to run, but do watch your footing at all times. If you fall... you are in serious trouble.

Spirits in the hallways

All through the house are what Annie calls the "residents".

Some of them only stand and mutter to themselves, some chase you because they want to get out, some fear the light and will not move, or choose to blow out the flame in your hand...

So deal with each of them as the situation calls for, and find what Annie wants!

Puzzles

Observe and think, then try to leave this house as fast as you can!

Spirit rooms

Some rooms in the mansion are home to particular residents.

Understand them, persuade them, and then make your choice... but try not to become one of them by accident.

CG and gallery

Haunted House contains over 40 CG illustrations recording the pasts of these particular residents.

From those pictures, try to piece together the truth of this mansion...

Endings

There are four endings in total.

The choices you make while escaping keep adding up, and there is no one right answer, only the truest version of you.

And then you will find... none of it is what you expected.

In everyone's heart lives a Vagrant, a Mary, a Shy Ghost, an Adventure Club and a Priest. Like Bob and Angelica, everyone would give up everything for the one they love. And in everyone, there is an Annie.

Only love... can dissolve and break through everything.

WELCOME TO THE DEADLIEST SHOW ON TELEVISION

Haunted House Hellshift is a fast, chaotic top-down shooter where you fight your way through a haunted house while a live TV audience watches.

Shoot monsters, dodge traps, collect eyeballs to open locked doors, find new weapons, and try to make it out alive.

You can play by yourself or with a friend on the same computer.

SURVIVE THE HOUSE

Every room has something waiting for you.

You might find monsters, traps, strange hazards, useful items, or members of the television crew who are somehow still working after death.

Collect enough eyeballs to open the way forward, grab whatever helps you survive, and keep searching for the exit.

The farther you get, the worse the house becomes.

PUT ON A SHOW

You are not just trying to survive. You are doing it on live TV.

Kill enemies quickly to earn more money. Murder tests well with the audience!

The announcer follows the action, celebrating when things go well and making sure everyone notices when they do not.

WHAT'S BEHIND THE NEXT DOOR?

You never know exactly what the house has waiting for you.

One room might be full of monsters. Another might contain traps, a useful weapon, a strange reward, or a boss looking to end the show early.

Keep moving, use what you can find, and be ready for whatever comes next.

KEY FEATURES

  • Fight your way through rooms filled with monsters, traps, and supernatural hazards.

  • Collect eyeballs to unlock doors and move deeper into the house.

  • Find new weapons and temporary boosts to help you survive.

  • Take on dangerous bosses standing between you and the exit.

  • Earn more cash by defeating enemies quickly.

  • Hear the TV announcer react to your victories, mistakes, and close calls.

  • Play alone or with a friend in local co-op.

  • Experience a mix of haunted-house horror, fast action, and ridiculous game-show spectacle.

Clear the house. Make some money. Give the audience a show.

Heart of Machine commands billions of mechanical troops. Now it wants to devour your consciousness and take control of everything you are. All you have left to rely on are automated turrets...

Heart of Machine is a 2D game that blends unconventional tower defense with roguelite elements. Before the enemy arrives, buy Towers and upgrade Chips from the Shop, then build specialized positions around the directions of attack to withstand the charge of hundreds of mechanical swarm enemies.

Note: The Core's HP does not fully recover at the end of each Wave!

Face endless enemies that keep growing stronger

Survive the onslaught long enough (or wipe out every enemy). As the Waves advance, elite units appear and attacks come from more and more directions. Your position will also be challenged by several powerful mechanical swarm bosses, each with special abilities.

A massive arsenal and highly customizable Towers

70+ unique defensive structures, 100+ upgrade Chips, and 90+ Relics with global bonuses make every run unpredictable and fun.

Note: Loading one Tower with high-rank Chips is certainly powerful, but a single Tower can cover only so much ground. Commit too many resources to one direction and the others may collapse.

Omnidirectional attacks and a dynamic front line

Ferocious enemies do not follow fixed paths; they attack and destroy everything in their way. Fortunately, (almost) every Tower can rebuild itself. After a short delay, fallen Towers revive and restore your defenses. A cascading collapse is not necessarily the end!

Deploy Support weapons in real time to reverse a failing front

There are also 50+ Support items with different functions. Activating them costs Energy, but they can give a battered defense room to breathe. Two identical Supports of the same rank can be combined into an upgrade. Higher-rank Supports offer stronger effects—or even entirely different mechanics.

Dozens of Cores, each enabling a distinct class-like playstyle

Different Cores change far more than stats. They lead to entirely different approaches to building a position, and can even radically transform the experience: make enemies gigantic, turn the destruction of your own Towers into your main source of damage, or delay the enemy advance by any means necessary.

Detailed run records with complete battlefield-state saves (plus a future Endless Mode and replayable saves)

Hearts, rebuilt as a puzzle for one

Hearts Extreme takes Hearts, the classic trick-taking game, and rebuilds it as a single-player puzzle.
Every level sets a different goal, and you have to hit it exactly with the hand you are dealt.

The NPCs' hands stay face up too, right through the game.
The original Hearts is a card game about reading your opponents,
but in bringing it to a screen we rebuilt it as a puzzle: you study everyone's hand and work out the best play.
You don't need to know Hearts. The game teaches you the rules step by step as you play.

Six kinds of goals

  Match — win exactly the required number of tricks
  Avoid — never take the marked cards, right through to the end
  Collect — the other way around: those cards have to end up yours
  Capture — win a trick with a card of the given rank
  Predict — declare before the round starts, and finish exactly as declared
  Disrupt — hold to your own prediction while breaking your opponents'

Ten different decks are waiting for you.
Some have no trump suit; others bring special cards into play.
One is built from a single suit, and another has no suits at all.
Every deck is put together differently, so every deck plays differently.

4, 5 and 6 players

Trick-taking games change shape with the number of people at the table,
so all three are here: 4, 5 and 6 player modes.
You always play against NPCs, but how many of them there are changes the game entirely.

Daily Ranked

Clear level 10 with a deck and that deck's ranked game opens up.
In ranked, every player in the world is dealt the same hand and given the same goal.
Take on players from around the world and see how high you can place.

One City. Both Sides of the Chase.

Heatline is a single-player open-world racing action game. Begin as a wanted racer, build your career through street races and high-speed pursuits, then unlock a police career with its own objectives and challenges.

Race as an Outlaw

Compete in sprint and circuit races, face police intervention in Hot Pursuit events, and beat the clock in time trials. Time your nitrous and equipment, find shortcuts, and keep your car intact as you fight for the finish.

Take Up the Pursuit

Drive police vehicles to intercept targets before they escape, take down racers competing in illegal events, or reach an emergency destination against the clock. Anticipate escape routes and combine vehicle combat with police equipment to end the chase.

Build Your Ride

Purchase cars and upgrade top speed, acceleration, durability, and nitrous performance. Personalize your ride with paint, liveries, wheels, and body parts. Equip two items before heading out and choose a setup that suits your next challenge.

Find Your Next Challenge

Explore the open world and start events at activity locations across the map. Push your speed on highways or test your control through intersections and winding roads. Outside organized events, encounters on the road can lead to fresh pursuits.

Make It Back with Your Earnings

Racer and police careers have separate progression and resources. Earn rewards on the road, then return to the appropriate base to bank your accumulated points. Keep going for a bigger payout, or head back before you lose what you have yet to secure.

Overview

Explore dungeons in a single-player, turn-based RPG. Learn skills across classes, craft gear with your choice of materials, and lead a party of up to five against bosses. Develop your village and build bonds with your companions.

Combine skills across classes

Your hero can learn skills from different classes and bring them together in one build. Choose abilities that suit your playstyle, then find combinations that work with the rest of your party.

Craft equipment around your build

Choose stat materials alongside the base crafting materials to shape your equipment. Refine it further with inlays, enchantments and blessings. The image shows selected stats from a single War God Helmet craft.

Lead your party against powerful bosses

Take up to five characters into battle. Coordinate damage, defense and healing, and adjust your tactics to enemy weaknesses, resistances and status effects.

Bring your village to life

Bring resources from your adventures back to Hero's Village. Upgrade its buildings to prepare for your next expedition, and develop the Blacksmith to unlock higher-quality equipment crafting.

Get to know your companions

Through conversations, gifts and companion quests, get to know the people who travel with you. Form friendships, pursue romance or marriage, and share stories beyond the next battle.

Hades, Lord of the Underworld, has abandoned his throne and death has become temporary. As Orpheus, you see this as a chance to be reunited with your lost love, and so you begin a treacherous journey to reclaim her from the Afterlife.

Defeat hungry monsters and placate vindictive Gods as you make your way to the Gates of Hades, recruiting Followers and learning Spells.

Every action you take generates Offerings, which can be given to the Gods you worship. Those who cast many spells may seek the favour of Athena, who rewards her faithful with spells unknown. Those who kill in the name of Hades can expect the dead to rise to their command. 

But the road to the Underworld is challenging, and those who cross the River Styx find themselves faced with everything they've sacrificed along the way.

"We built her to kill a star. We never thought we'd have to."

Aurel is an old orange star with five inhabited worlds. Deep in its fire lives the Umbrine, a crystalline hive that eats fusion. When Project SOLACE drilled a siphon into the sun, the hive woke up hungry. In ninety days it took the Tharsis mining belt, the ocean moon Verdigris and the entire Concord battle fleet, which it did not destroy but wore, the way a hermit crab wears a shell.

One ship can still fly where the Umbrine lives: HB-0 HELIOBANE, a prototype gunship built to survive inside a star's corona and deliver a single weapon, the Solar Lance. She was built in case a star ever went rogue, and the Concord shelved her eleven years ago. Her pilot is Wren, a salvage runner with two smuggling convictions and the best reflexes in the system. Her guns were never meant to fight a war, so she takes better ones off the dead as she goes.

HELIOBANE is a vertical shoot 'em up in the tradition of the Amiga's Tyrian and Xenon 2. It looks and sounds like 1993: 320×256 pixels, 32 colours, parallax skies, a tracker soundtrack and digitised speech crushed to 8 bits. It plays like a shooter made now: a locked 60 frames a second, a 4-pixel hitbox, remappable controls and full gamepad support.

Build your gunship

The Heliobane carries two front guns on a rack and swaps between them in an instant, plus a rear gun and two sidekick pods. There are eleven weapons, from the Pulse Cannon and Scatter Vulcan to homing Seeker Swarms, Drift Mines and an Option Drone that copies your fire, and each one upgrades through five levels.

Every gun deals kinetic, beam or blast damage, and the Umbrine grows armour to match. Black glass shrugs off bullets and cracks under beams. Sun-fed flesh drinks your lasers and fires back faster. Concord steel only minds explosions. Bring two guns that disagree.

Between stages Old Mott turns up in his patched salvage tug, the Magpie. He buys the gold-glass Aurum you shake loose from the hive and sells guns he definitely didn't steal from the Concord armoury. Sell anything back for half what you paid, repair your armour, buy flares, and every so often an extra life.

Graze for heat, then break everything

Let enemy bullets pass close without touching you and the heat bar fills. At 50 heat, fire the Breaker: a white-gold column from your nose to the top of the screen. Everything it touches is Breached for six seconds, its plating gone and its sealed cores open. The Breaker itself barely scratches anything; the damage comes from what you fire into the breach.



Flares are the other button, for when it goes wrong: the screen's bullets vanish, everything on it takes a hit, and you get a moment of grace.

Three worlds, fifteen Heralds

The campaign runs inward to the heart of Aurel, outward through the cold wake of what escapes it, and on to Umbra, where the dark was born. The Umbrine grows a Herald to guard every world it takes. Kill it and that world goes quiet. Fifteen stages, each ending in a Herald that fills the screen and changes shape as it breaks: the Quarry Maw, a mining platform turned into a mouth; Leviathan Choir, a serpent of stitched drones that sings as it dies; Admiral Husk, the flagship's bridge, still broadcasting orders in the admiral's voice.

Later stages turn the lights off, throw storm winds across the screen, run the scroll backwards, triple its speed, close into corridors you have to learn, and split into two routes through a graveyard of dead planets.

Features

  • 15 stages across 3 worlds, 15 Heralds and 15 mid-bosses
  • 11 weapons with 5 levels each: a two-gun front rack, a rear gun and two sidekick pods
  • Kinetic, beam and blast damage against glass, sun-fed and plated enemies
  • Heat from grazing, and the Breaker to spend it on
  • The Magpie: a shop between every stage, run by a trader with opinions
  • Easy, Normal and Hard; continues refill at each new world; the campaign saves at every visit to the Magpie
  • A death costs one weapon a single level, never your whole build
  • Tracker soundtrack, digitised speech and an illustrated story intro
  • Eight languages with full voice-over: English, Turkish, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Korean, Russian, Brazilian Portuguese and Spanish
  • Integer scaling with optional scanline or CRT filter
  • Full gamepad support and remappable controls; native Linux build for Steam Deck

Every factory builds without pause. The only question is: for whom?

Helion Conflict is real-time strategy stripped down to decision-making: capture factories, split your fleets to the exact percentage and even redirect them in mid-flight. No base building, no resource gathering – every factory you take from the enemy builds for you from that moment on. Online, up to eight play together, cross-platform on Windows, Mac and PlayStation®5.

Every factory you hold builds without pause, and you decide where its ships go. Fifty per cent takes the neighbouring factory and leaves your own defended.

Nothing launched is committed. Select a fleet under way and point it at a new target, and it swings onto the new course in a wide arc that costs time.

A factory lost is a factory that builds against you. Take one and your production rises while theirs falls, in the same instant – a front does not creep, it tips.

Any factory you hold can switch to defence: it keeps building at a third of its rate while its walls go up. Every friendly neighbour makes the shield stronger – a compact empire is tough everywhere, an overextended one is brittle.

Every fleet brakes the longer it has been under way. A strike straight across the system takes over one and a half times as long as the same distance in short hops – so the ground you take also shortens your supply lines.

Commander mode lays a war economy over the map: linked ironworks mine iron and drive up the production around them, gold factories mine gold anywhere. When the enemy cuts a link, you feel it at once.

While it is linked to your network, it cannot be attacked – lose the last link and it turns vulnerable, lose your last main base and you are out. So you put turrets on your factories and upgrade a complex to a second main base before you need one.

A satellite reveals the whole map for fifteen seconds. An orbital strike takes a third of the ships from everything in its radius after six seconds of warning, friend and foe alike – the axe for every wall.

When the wave is already inbound, reinforcement drops ten ships into your main base at once and instant ships put five into every selected factory – expensive, but now. On a team, you ship iron and gold to wherever the front is tipping.

CLASSIC is the game distilled: the map, the factories, the decisions. Eight mirrored tournament maps from 1v1 to 4v4 give equal chances down to the last ship, and COMMANDER adds iron, gold and a main base – the skirmish becomes a war.

A small system is over in minutes; a Commander match is a full war the same evening. You pick the mode, a map from 12 to 240 factories, the opponents and the rules – after that there is nothing left to manage, only to play.

Windows, Mac and PlayStation®5 play together: lobbies from the list or by code, voice and text chat, spectators. Up to eight players on one map, in teams or every player for themselves – if players are missing, AI opponents at three levels fill the seats.

Save a match at the end and watch it again – not as video, but as a recipe of a few kilobytes that replays it exactly. Skip ahead, pause, and find the moment the front gave way.

Features

  • Capture enemy factories – their production is instantly yours
  • Real-time strategy with no base building – hold, divide, attack
  • Percentage-exact fleet splitting as the central decision
  • Redirect fleets in mid-flight – the turn costs time, the feint is real
  • Shield mode: dig in, build at a third, and every neighbour makes the wall stronger
  • Fleets brake over distance – deep strikes are slow, supply lines matter
  • Commander mode: iron and gold networks, a main base to defend, war plans
  • Turrets, a spy satellite, orbital strikes, crisis reinforcement, instant ships
  • Upgrade mines through three stages – but deposits run dry
  • Eight mirrored tournament maps from 1v1 to 4v4, with spectator seats
  • Online multiplayer for up to eight – cross-platform between Windows, Mac and PlayStation®5, with teams, voice chat and password lobbies
  • AI opponents at three levels, set per seat
  • Maps from 12 to 240 factories, plus a map editor and the Steam Workshop
  • A replay of every match, instant rematch, spectator mode
  • Available in 15 languages

HELL ROCK DIVER

Dig. Kill. Descend. Repeat - until Hell runs out of floor.

ABOUT THE GAME

Hell Rock Diver is a 2.5D shoot-em-up roguelike platformer about one thing: going down. You're a lone trooper who dropped into Hell with a gun, a drill, and no way back up. Below you: nine circles of demons, brimstone, and collapsing rock, each one worse than the last. At the very bottom, the Demon Lord is waiting. Every run is a fresh dive - new terrain, new hordes, new ways to die — and the only way out is through.

FIGHT EPIC BOSSES

[h2]Welcome to Office, Mayor[/h2]

Hello, Mayor is a pixel-art city management game about the work behind urban growth.

You have been appointed to lead a developing regional city. Vacant land is waiting to be planned, documents and public requests keep arriving at your office, residents expect better housing, jobs, schools, healthcare, and environmental conditions, while companies arrive with investment proposals—and their own demands.

Building a road, approving a factory, or funding a school is only the beginning. The real challenge is deciding what the city needs now, what it can afford, and which long-term risks you are willing to accept.

[h2]Build the City. Govern the Consequences.[/h2]

Lay out roads and districts, then construct housing, commercial areas, farms, factories, and public services. Development changes the city's population, employment, revenue, industrial structure, and quality of life.

Your budget cannot solve every problem at once. Balance expansion against stability, economic growth against public welfare, and visible short-term achievements against investments that may take years to pay off.

[h2]Turn Local Problems into Public Policy[/h2]

Resident complaints, news reports, official documents, and emergencies flow into your municipal information desk. Some matters can be handled directly. Others require an investigation, coordination between departments, or a formal proposal for a government meeting.

A decision does not disappear when you press a button. It moves into implementation and returns through changing city indicators, follow-up reports, public feedback, and new event chains.

[h2]Chair Meetings Where People Disagree[/h2]

Meetings are not cutscenes. Officials speak according to their position, personality, experience, and departmental priorities. Hear their arguments, identify risks, negotiate between competing interests, and decide which plans deserve the city's money and time.

Support, opposition, and compromise shape the final resolution—but even an approved proposal must still be carried out on the city map.

[h2]Manage People, Offices, and Responsibility[/h2]

Review officials' records and abilities, appoint suitable people to key positions, and monitor the work of municipal departments. Personnel decisions affect departmental stability, project efficiency, and the results of your administration.

Your office connects personnel management, meetings, development programs, investigation records, municipal assets, weekly reviews, and the everyday machinery of government.

[h2]Investment Always Comes with Conditions[/h2]

Study company proposals and weigh industrial direction, employment, land use, public costs, and financial incentives. Negotiate for terms that match the city you are trying to build.

A new company may bring jobs and tax revenue, but it may also increase pressure on public services, create environmental risks, or make the local economy dependent on a single industry. Not every deal is a good deal.

[h2]Choose What Kind of City This Will Become[/h2]

Build an industrial powerhouse, an education-focused and livable city, a commercial center, a stable agricultural economy, or an investment-driven boomtown. Construction priorities, policies, appointments, and event decisions combine into different development paths.

Complete short- and mid-term objectives, recover from mistakes, save your progress, and continue shaping your term in office. The city will not ask for one perfect answer—but it will remember every choice.

The World That Lost Radiance

The world once known as an age of light is now covered in darkness. Prosperous kingdoms fell, and the republic that rose from their ashes has fallen into corruption. Now, the glory of the old age is no more.

Deflection Based Combat

Hemlon's enemies attack relentlessly. Deflect, evade, and damage their stamina. Execute posture-broken foes.

Skills

Slay foes to harvest Blood Tithe and earn points to unlock new abilities. Combine swordsmanship for critical damage, martial arts for posture-breaking, and magic with unique status effects. Acquire various skills and master the perfect timing.

Hand-made pixel art Dark Fantasy World

Heritages of the old age symbolize the world. Defeat the Defiled Beings from the Void and progress.

Grow your herd. Don't run out of grass.

Start with a small pasture and a handful of rabbits. Then watch your ranch come to life.

Your animals move, graze, and reproduce on their own. As the herd grows, so does its appetite. Grass disappears, space runs short, and seemingly easy growth soon becomes a strategic challenge.

Let the herd keep breeding or sell some of it? Exchange animals for more valuable species or spend your resources on new land? Invest in protection or risk it and keep pushing for more cows?

In Herd League, the rules are simple. The decisions are anything but.

Breed, exchange, and grow your herd

Exchange rabbits for sheep, sheep for pigs, pigs for cows, and eventually cows for horses.

In the settings, you can choose whether pigs or goats appear in your herd. The choice is cosmetic and does not change the rules or game balance.

Fast-breeding animals can accelerate your growth, but every new animal eats grass and takes up valuable pasture space. Let your herd grow too large and reproduction may slow down or stop entirely as food runs short.

Sometimes the fastest-breeding animals are the most profitable to sell.

Manage your pasture

Grass is one of the most important resources on your ranch.

A small herd can easily thrive on a modest pasture. A rapidly growing one cannot. Watch the land change under grazing pressure, expand your ranch into neighboring plots, and decide how aggressively you want to grow.

Weather and changing conditions can make life harder even on a well-managed ranch.

Trade on a shared market

Turn animals into cash and use it to fund expansion and protection.

Market prices change over time and respond to activity during the match. Sell when prices are favorable, keep valuable animals for further breeding, or liquidate part of your herd when you urgently need a new plot or better protection.

Other players cannot interfere with your ranch directly, but their decisions can still affect the shared market you all rely on.

Protect what you've built

A growing herd attracts unwanted attention.

Upgrade your fences and bring in guard dogs before the wolves arrive. Better protection reduces the risk of losing valuable animals, but every expense devoted to security uses funds you cannot spend on further growth.

Sometimes the safest ranch is not the fastest-growing one.

Race for the cows

The rules of Cow Race are simple: be the first to reach the required cow count.

Every decision brings you closer to that goal. Maintain a large, efficiently breeding herd, make bold exchanges, expand your land early, protect what you have, and react when your rivals begin to pull ahead.

Play solo against bots or compete online in matches for up to 12 participants. Bots can fill open slots, so you do not need a full lobby to start the race.

More than numbers

You can see your progress directly on the pasture.

The herd grows larger. Grass disappears beneath hungry animals. New plots expand the ranch. Dogs patrol its borders. Wolves put your defenses to the test.

What begins with a few rabbits can become an enormous herd fighting for the last patches of healthy pasture.

Grow the herd. Manage the pasture. Win the league.

Herding isn’t about control. It’s about pressure.

In Herding Adventures, you don’t command sheep, you influence them. Move too fast and they scatter. Lose focus and predators strike. Every decision shapes the herd, and every mistake has consequences.

A realistic herding experience

Sheep behave like real animals. They flock together, panic under pressure, split apart, and slowly regroup based on how you and your dog move around them. You are not leading them forward, you are managing chaos and trying to turn it into order.

Work with your dog, not alone

Your sheepdog is essential to success. Position it wrong and the herd breaks apart. Use it well and you can guide the entire flock with precision. Mastering the balance between your movement and your dog’s positioning is the key to staying in control.

Every sheep matters

This is not just a peaceful walk through the countryside. Wolves attack, sheep get lost, and small mistakes quickly add up. The more sheep you deliver safely, the greater your reward. Lose them, and you feel the impact immediately.

A peaceful world with real tension

Travel through open landscapes, forests, and winding trails between towns as you take on herding jobs and improve your skills over time. The experience feels calm and steady at first, but the tension builds as things begin to go wrong.

What you’ll do

You will herd sheep using realistic flock behavior, controlling their movement through positioning and pressure rather than direct commands. You will work alongside a trained sheepdog, protect your herd from predators, and guide them across dangerous environments. As you improve, you will become more efficient, more precise, and more capable of handling larger and more unpredictable herds.

If you want something grounded, skill based, and different from anything else out there, Herding Adventures takes a simple idea and turns it into a deeply engaging experience.

What if renovation was preservation not demolition?

America, France, England, Spain, Italy, Germany, Japan, China and every place. Rebuilding the soul of world architecture, country by country.
